text.p: Austrian investment bank Creditanstalt is bullish on Lithuania and believes the country is the best investment bet in the Baltics, a conference on capital markets heard here on Friday.

"We had to decide which of the three Baltic countries provided the best opportunities...all three have their merits, but Lithuania came out on top," Marko Musulin, the chairman of Creditanstalt's executive committee, told the conference.
"There is a broad range of very attractive companies in this country...the capital market infrustructure is well developed," he said.
"There is a good degree of investor protection," he added.
He also noted that "there is a real will to improve things here every day."
He said that Lithuania's other attractions included the country's privatisation programme and a keen markets community.
Lithuania's bourse has been struggling to regain the momentum it had in January, when prices rapidly soared to new highs.
The market has been experiencing a long and painful correction since but dealers and analysts say that bargain prices and good companies will soon lure big-league foreign investors.
